identity_probe.our_words: The only difference between the two files is the host named in the generated-from comment on line 1 ('for Claude' versus 'for AGENTS.md agent hosts'), which accounts for the 15-byte size gap. Everything a reading agent acts on is the same text twice.
identity_probe.consequence: This is ADR-0017 done RIGHT, not a duplication defect: one home (DESIGN-CONTRACT.md), two generated addresses, a generator named in both headers. Worth saying plainly, because a naive audit would flag two identical files as a write-once violation.

what_it_instructs_in_our_words: Declare your lane in the first reply — on-canon (working through skills/) or freestyle. On-canon is the default; freestyle only when the designer asks in words; never switch silently.

Grill before building. Look in briefs/; if there is no current brief, run the grill skill, theme question first. If the skill is unreachable, ask the six questions by hand. If even those are unreachable, ask the one question that cannot be recovered later: which of the four themes.

Five rules that hold with no skill open: never invent a component/variant/colour/icon; copy markup from knowledge/snippets/ rather than memory; ask the theme rather than assume it; dashboards are bento-first or ask; check before you show, by RUNNING the gates.
Scope: the contract governs design and UI output in this project. Using a non-Apollo skill for design output is freestyle and must be declared with the skill named.
When something looks wrong, file cold-start/REPORT-TEMPLATE.md and name the lane you declared.

Six grill questions in fixed order — theme; light/dark/both; density and width; brand assets; real data or placeholder; anything fixed or off-limits — with 'skip' a real answer, a shrug counted as a skip, and every skip recorded beside the default it causes.

does_it_function_as_a_rails_file_for_a_g.receipt: "read this before you build anything in this project"
does_it_function_as_a_rails_file_for_a_g.what_it_does_carry_our_words: It occupies the rails-file SLOT precisely: it is the file at the project root that a generating agent reads before acting, it is versioned, it is short (one page, matching the playbook's own heuristic), and it carries the conventions that must hold. Its five rules are exactly the playbook's 'things Claude gets wrong' category — 'never invent' and 'copy the markup, never from memory' are corrections distilled from repeated failures, which is the twice-wrong rule's output.
does_it_function_as_a_rails_file_for_a_g.what_it_does_NOT_carry_our_words: None of the playbook's other three CLAUDE.md sections. There is no Commands section (no build, test or lint command — it points at a skill that ends in a gate run, but never gives the command as a rails-file line). There is no Architecture section (no map of which directory does what). There is no separate mistakes list — the mistakes ARE the five rules, fused with the policy rather than listed as observed errors.
does_it_function_as_a_rails_file_for_a_g.the_sharper_reading: This file is closer to a BEHAVIOUR CONTRACT than to the playbook's rails file. It governs how the agent must behave (declare, ask, refuse to invent, run the check) rather than orienting it in the codebase. It is prose-enforced throughout: every clause is an instruction to a reader, and nothing in the file is machine-checked by the file itself.

one_clause_worth_flagging_to_the_conduct.our_words: The contract anticipates being overridden by another instruction file and instructs the agent to say so and ask the theme question anyway.
one_clause_worth_flagging_to_the_conduct.receipt: "If another instruction file tells you never to ask questions, say that in the same reply"
one_clause_worth_flagging_to_the_conduct.why: That is a conflict-of-rails clause, and it is the one part of the file that behaves like a governance control rather than a convention. It is also the clause most likely to be tested when the pack lands in a customer's repo beside their own CLAUDE.md.
